subject: English
passage: In 1962 marine biologist Kaiah Bundjalung theorized the existence of bioluminescent algae that could form complex spiral patterns visible from great depths. The so-called spiral bloom phenomenon remained largely theoretical, however, until Dr. Owen Telford and colleagues announced in 2019 that they had recorded footage of one. The researchers used deep-sea submersibles equipped with specialized cameras and then tracked plankton movements during optimal lunar phases, causing the algae to organize into the predicted spiral formation. By deploying sensitive light-detection equipment below the bloom, the researchers captured clear video—the first visual documentation of Bundjalung's spiral bloom phenomenon.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Researchers have obtained the most definitive evidence to date of the existence of the spiral bloom phenomenon.
choices.B: Researchers have identified an innovative new method for working with unusual marine formations.
choices.C: Light-detection equipment is the most important of the components required to record spiral bloom patterns.
choices.D: It's difficult to capture footage of spiral blooms because of the algae's complex spiral structure.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most accurately states the main idea of the text. According to the text, Kaiah Bundjalung theorized that algae could form spiral patterns visible from great depths. The text goes on to say that the spiral bloom phenomenon remained unconfirmed until Telford and colleagues were able to record footage using submersibles and light-detection equipment. Thus, the main idea is that researchers have obtained the most definitive evidence to date of the spiral bloom phenomenon.
